## Code review — `syncticket` backend

Scope: REST API, comments (focused), tickets, errors, config, tests vs `spec/`.

### High

**1. Comment list N+1 queries**  
`CommentMapper.toResponse` calls `comment.getTicket().getId()` on lazy `ManyToOne`. Each row in `findByTicketIdOrderByCreatedAtAsc` can trigger extra `SELECT` on `ticket`.

```10:16:d:\Code\JVM\syncticket\backend\src\main\java\com\syncticket\mapper\CommentMapper.java
    public CommentResponse toResponse(Comment comment) {
        return new CommentResponse(
                comment.getId(),
                comment.getTicket().getId(),
```

Fix direction: `@EntityGraph` / join fetch on list query, or expose `ticket_id` without loading `Ticket`.

**2. Ticket list N+1 comment counts**  
`TicketService.list` runs `commentRepository.countByTicketId` per row in page. Large pages hurt latency.

```75:77:d:\Code\JVM\syncticket\backend\src\main\java\com\syncticket\service\TicketService.java
        List<TicketSummaryResponse> content = result.getContent().stream()

```

**3. Comment API untested vs spec**  
`spec/test-strategy.md` §4.2 requires comment `PATCH`/`DELETE`, `409` on `CLOSED`, list behavior. No `Comment*` tests under `backend/src/test`. Only `TicketStatusTransitionIT` (3 cases) and `TicketStatusTest`. Gap for FR-06, FR-14, FR-15, BR-07.

**4. Flyway dev migrations on default profile**  
`application.yml` loads `classpath:db/migration/dev` always. `V4__seed_hundred_tickets.sql` runs outside explicit dev profile. Idempotent guard helps; still wrong for prod deploy unless profile overrides locations.

---

### Medium

**5. Integration coverage far below test strategy**  
Missing: invalid transition matrix (19 pairs), happy paths, stale `version`, `PATCH` with `status`, comment flows, `allowedTransitions` on GET. Regressions on state machine easy to miss.

**6. `CommentNotFoundException` uses `TICKET_NOT_FOUND`**  
```45:48:d:\Code\JVM\syncticket\backend\src\main\java\com\syncticket\exception\GlobalExceptionHandler.java
    @ExceptionHandler(CommentNotFoundException.class)
    public ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail> handleCommentNotFound(CommentNotFoundException ex, HttpServletRequest request) {
        ProblemDetail problem = problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, ErrorCode.TICKET_NOT_FOUND, ex.getMessage(), request);
```

Matches `api-contract.md` §4.8 for HTTP 404. Clients cannot distinguish missing ticket vs wrong `commentId` on path except `detail` text. OK for v1 if documented; brittle for UI error routing.

**7. No auth (accepted v1 risk)**  
`requirements.md` A-01: no auth; `author` is free text. Not a bug vs spec. Public network deploy = anyone can read/write all tickets and impersonate authors. Document deployment boundary.

**8. Catch-all `Exception` handler**  
```86:95:d:\Code\JVM\syncticket\backend\src\main\java\com\syncticket\exception\GlobalExceptionHandler.java

    public ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail> handleUnexpected(Exception ex, HttpServletRequest request) {
```

Can mask framework errors that deserve dedicated handling (e.g. some `DataAccessException`). Body stays generic; logs OK.

---

### Low

**9. Comment controller vs project `.cursorrules`**  
No `ApiResponse` wrapper, no per-method try/catch. Matches actual `ProblemDetail` + `@RestControllerAdvice` design and `api-contract.md`. Rules file stale, not runtime bug.

**10. `POST` comment has no `Location` header**  
Tickets use `201` + `Location`. Comments use `201` + body only. Fine if contract does not require `Location`.

**11. `UpdateCommentRequest` / `CreateCommentRequest` lack `@JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown = true)`**  
`UpdateTicketRequest` has it. Boot default usually ignores unknown JSON; inconsistent with §5 cross-cutting intent for ticket updates only.

**12. `CommentService` ↔ `TicketService` layering**  
Comments always load ticket via `ticketService.findTicket` + `ensureEditable`. Correct for BR-07. `list` only checks ticket exists; read on terminal ticket allowed — matches §4.6.

---

### What looks solid

- Comment scoped by `findByIdAndTicketId` — no cross-ticket ID leak.
- Terminal ticket guard on add/update/delete via `ensureEditable()`.
- Validation + trim on comment DTOs; ProblemDetail errors aligned with contract.
- Optimistic locking on tickets (`version` + handler).
- `TicketSpecifications.escapeLike` for search wildcard safety.
- `open-in-view: false` — good with lazy associations (mapper still triggers lazy loads).

---

1. `CommentIT`: create → list order → patch body → delete → 404 wrong `commentId`.
2. Close ticket → `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` comment → `409 TICKET_NOT_EDITABLE`.
3. Comment list on closed ticket → `200` (read-only).
4. Performance follow-up: fetch/count tests or query logging on list endpoints.

---

**Summary:** Logic for comments and editability matches spec. Main risks: **N+1 on comment and ticket lists**, **missing comment integration tests**, **dev Flyway path on default config**. Security gaps are in-scope for v1 but matter for deployment.

## Code review (post N+1 + comment IT fixes)

Prior review items **1–3** look addressed. Remaining findings below.

---

### High

**1. State-machine IT still thin vs `spec/test-strategy.md` §4.2**  
`TicketStatusTransitionIT` has 3 cases. Spec still wants: all 6 valid transitions, 19 invalid pairs, full happy paths, stale `version`, `PATCH` with `status`, `allowedTransitions` on GET per status, `CANCELLED` edit rules.  
`TicketCrudIT` + `CommentApiIT` help CRUD/comments; **state machine regression risk** remains main gap.

**2. No test for batched `commentCount` on list**  
`TicketService.list` uses `countGroupedByTicketId`. No unit or IT asserts `commentCount` on paged list after multiple comments. Batch query or mapping bug could slip through.

---

### Medium

**3. `TicketStatusTransitionIT` package vs path**  
File: `com/syncticket/ticket/api/`. Package: `com.syncticket.controller`. Javac may still compile; IDE/refactor tools break. Align package with directory.

**4. Three IT classes, three Postgres containers**  
`TicketStatusTransitionIT`, `TicketCrudIT`, `CommentApiIT` each declare `@Container static PostgreSQLContainer`. Full `integrationTest` starts **3** DBs. Slow CI; consider shared base class or single container per JVM.

**5. `countGroupedByTicketId` uses raw `Object[]` casts**  
```175:181:d:\Code\JVM\syncticket\backend\src\main\java\com\syncticket\service\TicketService.java
        return commentRepository.countGroupedByTicketId(ticketIds).stream()
                .collect(Collectors.toMap(row -> (Long) row[0], row -> (Long) row[1]));
```  
`COUNT` may be `Long` or `Integer` by provider. Safer: `((Number) row[1]).longValue()`. Low chance on PostgreSQL + Hibernate 6, still brittle.

**6. `CommentList` delete path skips ticket refresh on `TICKET_NOT_EDITABLE`**  
Add/patch call `onTicketRefetch()` when ticket became terminal. `handleDelete` only `alert()` — UI can show edit/delete after race if status changed elsewhere.

**7. Terminal copy says “closed” for `CANCELLED`**  
`isTerminalStatus` includes `CANCELLED`. Message: “This ticket is closed…” — misleading for cancelled tickets (UX, not API bug).

**8. No auth (v1 by design)**  
Still open API if exposed beyond trusted network. See `requirements.md` A-01.

---

### Low

**9. `CommentNotFoundException` → `TICKET_NOT_FOUND`**  
Matches `api-contract.md` §4.8. Clients rely on `detail` text to tell ticket missing vs comment wrong.

**10. `CommentApiIT` JSON via `String.format`**  
Fine for fixed strings; breaks if test data has `"` or `\`. Use `ObjectMapper` for payloads.

**11. `CommentApiIT` omits `CANCELLED` mutation case**  
Only `CLOSED` covered; `CANCELLED` same BR-07 rule — one more test would mirror spec.

**12. `.cursorrules` vs codebase**  
Rules want `ApiResponse` + repository in controllers. App uses `ProblemDetail` + constructor injection. Doc drift only.

**2. No CI / quality gates from `spec/test-strategy.md` §6**

**3. No `@WebMvcTest` / `@DataJpaTest`**  
Spec pyramid expects web slice + repository IT. Only full `@SpringBootTest` + unit tests. Validation edge cases (AC-12 boundaries, bad query `status`) mostly untested at HTTP/DB slice level.

**4. `countGroupedByTicketId` mapping still brittle**  
```180:181:d:\Code\JVM\syncticket\backend\src\main\java\com\syncticket\service\TicketService.java

                .collect(Collectors.toMap(row -> (Long) row[0], row -> (Long) row[1]));
```  

`COUNT` may not always be `Long`. IT on PostgreSQL passes today; cast can break on provider change. Prefer `((Number) row[1]).longValue()`.
